text: A password is a secret word that keeps your things private. Most phones and apps ask for one, and the best ones are long and different for every account. People change a password when they think someone has seen it, or just once in a while. They say things like, change my password, make it stronger, or lock my phone after one minute. A phone can also hide messages on the lock screen, so a person at your lunch table cannot read them. Some people slice the risk in half by turning on a second check, like a code sent by text. At a minimum, use a screen lock. You can also ask, who can see my photos, and the assistant shows the sharing list.

Priya was a student, and the wifi in her flat kept dropping. A big storm had just passed, and the router light was blinking red. She sat at her desk, on the chair with the broken wheel, and said to her phone, 'Restart router.' The assistant understood that she meant the router in the hall. It sent the restart command and told her it would take about two minutes. Priya needed to send her essay to her teacher, so she waited. When the light turned green, she said, 'Email my essay to Mr. Dale.' The assistant found the file called essay final, attached it, and sent the email. It told her the message had gone out. Priya smiled and went back to studying.

name: wind_down_timer
does: Starts a calm bedtime routine that dims the lights, plays soft sounds, and stops them when the person falls asleep.
inputs: the time the person wants to be asleep and the kind of sound they like
people say:
- I want to be asleep by ten thirty
- help me relax, my head is full of thoughts
- it's still bright outside, make my room dark for bed
- I just had a shower, now I need to calm down
- play rain sounds until I drift off
- I put my paper book down, time to sleep

Mrs. Alvarez was a retired teacher who read one long novel every July. One evening she sat in her chair with a cup of lemon tea that tasted too sour. 'I don't want the next chapter tonight,' she said to the smart speaker, 'and please don't read it out loud. Just keep my place.' The assistant understood that she wanted to save her spot and not play the audiobook. It put a bookmark at page 212, the end of chapter nine, and said the bookmark would carry over to her phone as well. Mrs. Alvarez nodded. She finished her tea, turned off the light, and the speaker stayed quiet all night.

Tom had just moved to the city with his two kids. After a long day standing at the school gate in the cold March wind, his feet were sore. That evening he told the family tablet, 'Give the kids half an hour less screen time on school nights.' The assistant understood that he wanted the nightly limit to be shorter by thirty minutes. The old limit was ninety minutes, so it changed it to sixty. It told Tom the new limit was one hour and that it would start tonight. Tom said that was fine, and he also asked it to read the kids a bedtime story if they finished early. The assistant said yes and set the story for eight o'clock.

Luis drove a school bus, and on a rainy morning he sat in the parking lot with a wool scarf around his neck, waiting for the first stop. It had snowed last week, and the roads were still slick. He spoke to his phone: 'Excuse me, could you please remind me tonight at eight about my daughter's science project, because it is due on Friday and last time I forgot and she was very upset?' The assistant understood that Luis wanted one reminder, tonight at eight, about the science project. It made the reminder, wrote science project, due Friday, and told him it was set. Luis thanked it and started the engine.

Finding a film to watch is easy now. A phone or TV can list what is on at the cinema near you, show trailers, and tell you the times. People use it to pick a movie before they leave home. You can change the day, the place, or the kind of film. They say, show me something funny for tonight, or what's on Saturday afternoon. If the first choice is not right for the kids, they say, replace that one with a cartoon. At home, some people switch off the lamp so the room is dark before the trailer starts. Families also ask for a safe film for young children, and the assistant looks at the age rating.

Nina was nine, and the air in her room felt dry and smelly. Her neighbor was burning leaves in the yard, and the smoke was drifting in. She stood by her bed and said, 'Can you turn on the humidifier and close the north window?' The assistant understood that she wanted two things done: the humidifier on, and the window shut. It switched on the humidifier in her room, and it asked the smart window to close. Nina asked if it could help the air get clean faster, so the assistant also started the purifier on its high setting. After a few minutes the room smelled fresh again. Nina said thank you and went back to her drawing.

name: gift_idea_finder
does: Suggests gift ideas for a person based on their age, hobbies and how much money you want to spend.
inputs: who the gift is for, what they like, and the budget
people say:
- what should I get my brother for his birthday
- my aunt is turning sixty and I'm out of ideas
- something under twenty dollars for a friend who loves anything blue
- my dad likes burgers and grilling, got any present ideas
- I need a gift for my cousin who lives far away

Sam was ten, and he wanted to show his friends his new dog. The dog, Biscuit, weighed forty pound and was chilling on the sofa in the sun. Sam took a picture and told the family tablet, 'Post this on our page tomorrow at seven.' The assistant understood that he wanted the photo shared, but not right now. It said that seven in the morning was a busy time on the page, so more people might see it. Sam said that was good. The assistant set the post for tomorrow at seven and told Sam it would show him the likes when they came in. Sam gave Biscuit a pat.

Meal planning means deciding what to eat for the week before you go shopping. It is a job that many families share. People use it to save money, eat better, and stop asking what's for dinner every night. You can change a plan whenever you like. Say, swap Tuesday's dinner for pasta, no fish this week, or make Friday bigger because we invite friends over. A rare treat, like pizza, can go on the weekend. Packed lunches are part of the plan too, so a parent might say, give the kids something cold for school on Monday. At the end, the plan turns into a shopping list.

A bill is a request for money for something you used, like electricity, water or rent. Each bill has an amount and a due date. The power bill may come in a purple envelope, or as a message on your phone. People change when and how they pay. They say, pay the water bill on the first, remind me three days before the rent is due, or take the electric bill off autopay. If a bill looks high, they ask how much they used last month. An old fridge plugged into the outlet in the garage can take a lot of power, so people sometimes find the reason this way. Paying on time keeps things simple.

Maya was late for work and grabbing her keys. The pollen count was high, and she had already taken her allergy dose that morning. As she hurried to the door she said, 'Run the purifier on full until tomorrow at seven, and cool the bedroom a little.' The assistant understood that she wanted the tall purifier in the hall set to its strongest level until seven the next morning. It also lowered the bedroom heat by two degrees. It told her both things were done. Maya said thanks over her shoulder and ran for the bus. When she came home that evening, the air in the flat felt fresh and clear.

Dana got home after a rough night shift. Her dog Pepper sat by an empty bowl, whining. The kitchen lamp was glaring in her tired eyes. 'It's way too bright in here, and Pepper's tummy is growling,' she mumbled. She needed a boost of sleep more than coffee. The assistant understood the hints. It dimmed the lamp to a soft glow, and it told the pet feeder to give Pepper his usual breakfast, one cup of food. It said both things out loud so Dana knew. Pepper ate happily, and Dana dropped onto the sofa. The assistant added that it would keep the house quiet until noon.

Hector was a gardener, and he loved the garden at night. He wanted to record a short video of the first star over the roses. 'Dim the porch light and start recording tomorrow at seven in the evening,' he told his phone. The assistant understood that two things were needed: the porch light should be lowered, and the camera should start filming at seven. The light was already dim, so it only lowered it a little more. It scheduled the recording for tomorrow at seven, and said the clip would save to Hector's video folder. Hector went inside for dinner, happy that the plan was ready.

Rosa was a cook, and her kitchen was loud. The washer was running in the back room, and her hands were covered in flour. She typed with one thumb: 'remind me my sisters birtday is close, find gift'. The assistant saw the small typo and understood what she meant. Her sister's birthday was in four days. It made a reminder for the day before, and it showed three gift ideas: a cookbook, a scarf, and a pack of fancy tea. Rosa said she liked the cookbook. The assistant added it to her shopping list and told her it would remind her to wrap it. Rosa wiped her hands and went back to the stove.

Omar owned a furniture shop that sold beds, and on Saturday he wanted to follow the football. 'Show me the score of the Hawks game,' he said to his phone. Then he stopped. 'No, sorry, I mean the Eagles game.' The assistant understood that he had changed his mind, so it dropped the Hawks and looked up the Eagles. It told him the Eagles were winning two to one at halftime. It was getting dark outside, and Omar still had to close up. He asked it to tell him the final score before he started to leave the shop. The assistant said it would send a message when the game ended.

A focus timer helps you work hard for a short time and then rest. A common plan is twenty-five minutes of work and then a five-minute break. During the break you stand up, stretch, and let your eyes rest, especially if they feel sore from the screen. Some people open a window or sit near a vent to get fresh air, or they blow on a hot cup of tea. People change the timer by saying, make it thirty minutes, give me a longer break, or start my morning routine at six. You can also ask for a gentle sound when time is up instead of a loud one. A good routine keeps the day calm and the work moving.

Ben was late for the airport, and his bag was half packed. His grandmother was coming to visit, and he could not remember how long he had left to get ready. 'Days until Sunday,' he said to his phone. The assistant understood that he wanted to know how many days remained before Sunday. It counted from today and said there were three days left. Ben nodded. He had thought tomorrow was the day, and he had paid for an expensive taxi for nothing. He canceled the taxi with a quick word to the assistant, and then he sat down to finish his packing in peace.

Mr. Okafor was a retired teacher, and on cold evenings he liked to sit in his cozy chair by the window. 'Would you please record the evening news on the third channel tonight and save it for me,' he said to the TV, 'because I will be at choir practice and my wife would like to see it later?' The assistant understood that he wanted the news on channel three recorded and kept. It set the recording for six o'clock, said it would track the show even if it started late, and told him where the video would be saved. Mr. Okafor thanked it and went to find his coat.

Lina owned a flower shop, and she had a call with her supplier at ten. She sat at the counter with her laptop and said, 'Join my ten o'clock call, and make the shared window twice as big.' The assistant understood the two parts. It opened the meeting link and made the shared window double its size so Lina could see the order list. When the sound was bad, the supplier said sorry for the noise. Lina asked the assistant for half the volume, and it turned the speaker down. She still did not understand one number on the list, so she asked the assistant to read it again, slowly. It did.

A drink can be made many ways, and most people like it a certain way. Coffee can be strong or weak, tea can be hot or iced, and a smoothie can be thick or thin. A student might pack a flask of gentle green tea for class, while a runner wants a sweet fruit smoothie. When people want a change, they say, make it stronger, less sugar, half sweet, or no ice. The machine or the assistant then changes the amount of coffee, milk or honey. It is for making a drink that tastes right, without starting over every time. Some people also ask for a smaller cup in the afternoon.

Jake was late, and the hiking trip started in an hour. He threw his boots into the car and told his phone, 'Make my packing list for two nights, and bring twice as much water as last time.' The assistant understood that he wanted the usual list, but with the water doubled. It listed a tent, a sleeping bag, snacks, and six bottles of water instead of three. His job was to carry the food, so it added a bag for that too. As he drove, the phone flashed a weather alert: sunny all weekend. The assistant told him to add sunscreen to the list, and Jake said yes.

They want to see a doctor tomorrow.
Visit doctor tomorrow
Can I see a doctor tomorrow at seven?
Book me in with Dr. Lee for tomorrow morning, please.
My throat is sore and vinegar tea did not help, so I want to visit the clinic tomorrow at seven.
Is there a free slot tomorrow around seven for a check-up?
I would like the earliest time tomorrow, and I'm not sure it is safe to wait longer.
Could you please find me an appointment at the health center for tomorrow at seven in the morning?
Get me a doctor, tomorrow, seven.
I know it is short notice, but is anyone free to see me tomorrow at seven?

Person: hey how much is it if i go west next winter
Assistant: Do you mean the price of a trip, or what your money is worth in another country?
Person: my money. i have 200 dollars and im going to ireland
Assistant: Got it. When do you want to exchange it? Rates change a little every day.
Person: tomorrow at seven, before i climb on the bus to the airport
Assistant: I can't know tomorrow's rate yet, but today's rate would give you about 185 euros. I can check again tomorrow morning.
Person: ok do that

A smart speaker is a small box that can hear you and answer. It plays music, tells the weather, sets timers and controls lights. Each person in the house can have a voice profile, so the speaker knows who is talking. If one speaker is not enough, you can group speakers so the same song plays in the kitchen and the living room. People change the volume by saying, turn it up, a bit quieter, or louder please. They ask what the speaker can do, and it lists its skills. If a person is hungry, they can ask for a recipe. Say, stop, and the speaker goes quiet. It listens closely only after it hears its wake word.

They want to know when the food will arrive.
Where's my food?
How long until the pizza is here?
Is the driver back at the restaurant or on the way to me?
My guests are about to be welcomed in, so is dinner nearly here?
Will it take more than twenty-five minutes?
Can you check the delivery and tell me the time it will get to my door?
I've been waiting a while. What's the new arrival time on my order?
Please let me know as soon as the delivery person is close, I'm starving.

Walter was not good with technology. His grandson had set up the email on a tablet that sat by the coat hook in the hall. One morning Walter wiped his dirty glasses on his sleeve and said, 'Unread mail?' The assistant understood that he wanted to know about new emails. It said there were four messages, and it read the names of the people who sent them. One was from the water company. Walter said, 'Label that one bills.' The assistant put a bills label on the email and moved it to a folder with the same name. Walter was pleased that it had been so easy, and he went to make toast.

Grace was not good with technology, and she did not like the clinic website, where she had tried to change her visit three times. So she pressed the button on her speaker and said, 'Move my dentist visit to Friday and tell me what is on Thursday.' The assistant understood both parts. It moved the visit from Wednesday to Friday at the same time, and it read out Thursday's plans: lunch with her sister at noon and a walk in the east park at four. Grace was surprised that two things had happened at once. She thanked the speaker, and the assistant said that she could ask for more changes any time.

Kofi had just moved to the city, and he felt silly asking a phone what to eat. But he had no plan and not much money. 'Plan dinners for the week,' he said, 'but no meat and nothing spicy.' The assistant understood that he wanted five dinners without meat and without hot peppers. It suggested rice with beans, vegetable soup, and a pasta bake. It said half of the recipes made enough for two meals, so he could stretch his budget by eating the rest the next day. Kofi liked that idea. He asked the assistant to turn the plan into a shopping list, and it did.

name: pantry_check
does: Tells you which foods at home are running low and puts them on the shopping list so the order can be sent with one click.
inputs: the name of the food, and any direction about which store to buy it from
people say:
- do we have any eggs left
- are we out of milk again
- what's getting low in the fridge
- the square tin on the shelf, is it empty
- we're almost done with rice, get more from the corner shop

Scaling a recipe means making more or less of a dish than the card says. Grandma's soup might serve four, but you have eight guests, so you need double. Cups, spoons and servings all change together. People say, make it for six, cut it in half, or I only need enough for one. The numbers change: two cups of rice become four, and a half spoon of salt becomes a whole one. Some people also say, wake me up when the soup is ready, and set a timer. It helps when the recipe uses cups but your measuring tool uses spoons, because the helper can change one to the other.

Joy was a nurse, and she had just finished a long night shift. She sat in her car and said, 'Scan the clinic website for the least busy day next week and remind me to take my afternoon dose at noon.' The assistant understood that there were two requests. It looked at the clinic page and saw that Tuesday had the fewest visits, so it offered Tuesday morning. It also set a reminder for noon with the words, take afternoon dose. Joy said to book Tuesday, and the assistant did. She drove home, glad that she did not have to remember anything herself.

They want to book a haircut.
Haircut, please.
I don't want a morning slot. Book a haircut after lunch.
Can you fit me in for a trim sometime this week, a total of an hour at most?
My current barber is booked up, so find another one nearby, but not downtown.
I need to plan a haircut before the wedding on Saturday, any open times?
Get me anything tomorrow, except the early hours.
I would be grateful if you could find a free time at the salon this week, and please do not choose a day when it rains.
When is the next free spot at the hair place?

A lawn needs cutting and water to stay healthy. Many yards now have a robot mower that goes over the grass by itself and a sprinkler that comes on at set times. The mower rests in its dock when it is done or when rain starts, because wet grass is hard to cut. People change the plan by saying, cut the grass shorter, skip tomorrow's watering, or mow only the front. If the ground is still damp, they ask to wait a day. Someone who bought a broken mower may ask the shop for a refund. Edges are trimmed with a small tool along paths and flower beds. A little care each week keeps grass green and thick.

name: bike_route_finder
does: Finds a bike route of the length and difficulty you want, and can cancel a ride you saved earlier.
inputs: where you start, how far you want to ride, and how hilly it can be
people say:
- my mother and I want an easy ride on Sunday
- small hills only, about ten miles
- cancel Saturday's ride, it's going to rain
- find me a loop that starts at the park
- how far is the lake trail from my house

They want to hear today's top headlines.
News.
Headlines please.
What's going on today?
Is there anything big in the news right now?
Read me the main stories, my hands are on the wheel.
I want to pay attention to the day's big stories while I make coffee, can you go through them?
If I'm lucky there's some good news today, so read me what you have.
Could you give me a quick summary of what happened this morning, please?

They want to know how much electricity the house is using.
Power use?
Energy now.
How much electricity are we using right now?
Sync the meter reading with my phone and show me what we used today.
We were away on holiday, did the house use much power?
The house is quiet and nobody is home, so why is the meter still running?
Could you tell me, as simply as you can, how our energy use compares with last week?
Show me my usage since this morning.

Amir had just moved to the city and was in his first apartment. He had cooked pasta, packed lunch for the next day, and turned down the brightness on his phone because his eyes were tired. Then he remembered that rent was coming. 'Move fifty dollars from savings to checking tomorrow at seven,' he said. The assistant understood that he wanted a transfer between his own two accounts at seven the next morning. It checked that savings had enough money, scheduled the move, and read the plan back to him. Amir said that was right. The assistant told him the transfer would show up in checking within a few minutes of seven.

name: game_night_scorekeeper
does: Keeps score for board games and card games, starts timers for turns, and says who is winning.
inputs: the names of the players, the game, and the points
people say:
- start a new game when my friends arrive
- I landed on the tax square, take two hundred from me
- who's winning right now
- give Sam a juicy bonus of ten points
- start a one-minute timer for my turn

They want to call a friend.
Call Mia.
Phone Dad on speaker, my hands are full on the stairs.
Ring my sister and let it ring for twenty seconds before voicemail.
Can you fit a call to Mom in before dinner?
Dial the number on the black card I saved, please.
I'd like to talk to Grandpa, could you start that call for me?
Get Mia on the line.
Please call my friend Joe and put him on speakerphone so everyone can hear.

Elena had just woken up, and her head was still full of sleep. She needed to board the early train, and she had installed a ride app last week. She mumbled to her phone, 'Book a ride to the station tomorrow at seven.' The assistant understood that she wanted a car for the next morning, not right now. It asked where to pick her up, and she said the usual place at the front door. It booked the ride and said the driver would arrive at ten to seven. Elena was glad. She pulled the blanket back over her head and went back to sleep for a little longer.

Leo was a student, and he sat on a bench in the sun with his headphones on. A woman beside him was laughing at something on her phone, and Leo remembered that his audiobook was funny too. 'Next chapter,' he said to his phone. The assistant understood that he was done with this chapter and wanted to hear the one after it. It skipped from chapter six to chapter seven and began to play. It also told him how long the new chapter was: twenty minutes. Leo smiled and leaned back, because that was just enough time before class.

Mia was eight, and she had a sore throat. She sat in bed with an electric blanket up to her chin. 'Please keep a note for Mom to take me to the doctor tomorrow at seven,' she told the family tablet. The assistant understood that Mia wanted a reminder for her mom about a doctor visit the next morning. It wrote the note and sent it to Mom's phone. Then it showed the route to the clinic on the screen, so Mom could see how long the drive would take. Mia said thank you in a small voice, and the assistant told her to drink some warm water and get some rest.

Person: Play podcast.
Assistant: Sure. Which podcast do you want?
Person: the cooking one, the crispy chicken show
Assistant: Found it. Do you want the newest episode, or where you stopped last time?
Person: where i stopped. i can only listen to half of it before the school run
Assistant: Okay. I'll play from minute twenty-two. Tell me when to stop and I will save your place.
Person: thanks, you're the best

A smart lock lets a front door open without a key. It can open with a code, a phone, or your voice. It is for keeping the home safe and for letting people in when you are not there. People change who can come in. They say, give my neighbor a code for today, lock the garage door, or tell me when the door opens. A camera at the door can upload a short video each time someone rings, so you see who is there. A person ironing in the back room can still see the visitor on a phone screen. The lock works well when the battery is fresh, so many locks warn you when it is low.

Sports are games with teams, scores and times. People follow a match to know who is winning and when the next one starts. An assistant can tell you the score, show the league table, or remind you when your team plays. People change what they follow by saying, add my son's team, tell me when the game starts, or stop alerts for hockey. If the match does not go well, a fan may ask where the team stands now. Training is part of sports too: a runner can ask for a new running direction, or a plan for ten minutes of stretching. Go with whatever team you love, and the updates will come to you.

Chen had just moved to the city and was ordering pastries for a small party. He wanted to be sure the price was right and the total was safe to pay. 'What is twelve times four?' he asked his phone. Then he frowned. 'No, wait, I mean twelve times five.' The assistant understood that he had fixed the number and answered the new question: sixty. Chen said that was the number of pastries he needed for his guests. He asked what the price would be at two dollars each. The assistant multiplied sixty by two and said one hundred twenty dollars. Chen sighed, then placed the order anyway.

News is a short list of the things that happened today. It can be about the world, your town, or your favorite team. People use it to stay informed without reading every paper. They change what they get by saying, only local news, no sports, or read me the headlines in the morning. If a story is long, they ask for a short version. Some stories make your head spin, so people ask for good news only. A weather story may say it will be cold tonight. Say, tell me more about that one, and the assistant reads the whole story. You can ask it to stop at any time, even before you blink.
